Iran International, liveblog 19 November 2026

Iran cannot overcome its current conditions while holding on to prewar expectations, President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Thursday.

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he and Chinese President Xi Jinping strongly support oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, speaking at the start of a meeting during the APEC summit in China.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's relocation to a military base was linked to Israeli intelligence about an alleged Iranian plot to use chemical agents against senior American officials, The New York Times reported Wednesday, citing a person briefed on the intelligence.

US President Donald Trump said Wednesday in an interview with Fox News that a preliminary agreement with Iran was “a waste of time,” pledging to end the war soon and seeking a lasting deal with Tehran.

US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that Washington does not need help from China or Russia to end the war with Iran, adding that Iranian officials want to reach an agreement.

US President Donald Trump is considering several options for further military action against Iran, including attacks on nuclear and missile facilities and a broader offensive targeting the country's senior leadership, Israel Hayom reported Wednesday, citing a senior non-Israeli diplomatic official.

“If we try to carry on with the same expectations and demands we had before the war, it will be impossible to get through the current situation,” he said.

He described the situation as more complex, saying Iran faced cultural and economic conflicts in addition to military conflict.

“They want to force us to surrender through blockade and sanctions,” Pezeshkian said. “We must continue with life and development while increasing our ability to withstand these pressures.”

100%Nov 19, 2026, 10:15 GMT+0Iran’s Guards say two supertankers hit mines, exploded in Strait of HormuzIran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said on Thursday that two supertankers hit naval mines and exploded while crossing a “restricted route” through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Guards’ public relations office said the vessels were carrying a combined total of more than 4 million barrels of crude oil and were burning near the strait’s southern coast.

It also claimed that the tankers had US fighter jet and surveillance drone support as they attempted to cross the route covertly, and were abandoned after hitting the mines.

A member of Iranian parliament’s national security committee said on Thursday that Israeli desalination plants are within range of Iran’s precision missiles, warning that any military action would draw a heavy response.

Aladdin Boroujerdi said some Israeli desalination plants were near the country’s nuclear power plant.

He also said US President Donald Trump had made a “historic mistake” under the influence of what he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s provocations.

100%Nov 19, 2026, 10:09 GMT+0Danger alert lifted in Saudi Arabia’s Najran RegionSaudi Civil Defense issued an all-clear for Najran Region on Thursday, after an earlier warning of danger. It urged residents to continue following safety instructions.

Workers at the Kaveh Soda Ash plant in Firuzabad, Fars province, continued their strike for a fourth consecutive day, demanding higher wages and protesting the lack of response from authorities.

Employees earn between 280 million and 300 million rials a month (approximately $105 to $112), far below what is needed to cover basic living expenses, with even a single person unable to make ends meet on such wages, a worker said in a message to Iran International.

The worker said management had told employees they could leave if they were unwilling to work for those wages and threatened to shut down the plant.

Around 3,000 workers face uncertainty over their livelihoods, with neither local officials nor the area's parliamentary representative responding to their demands, the worker added.

100%Workers at the Kaveh Soda Ash plant gather during a strike over low wages and working conditions in Firuzabad, Fars province, southern Iran.Nov 19, 2026, 09:25 GMT+0BREAKING NEWS US will not let Iran get nuclear weapon, Trump tells Putin and XiUS President Donald Trump told Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday that the United States would not allow Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon, during a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China.

“It’s vital that we cooperate to combat the threat of nuclear proliferation in other countries around the world,” Trump said. “That’s what we’re doing in Iran. We’re not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon.”

Trump also said that the United States, Russia and China were uniquely positioned to discuss reducing their nuclear arsenals and lowering the risk the weapons could be used.

Xi said the United States, China and Russia, as major powers and permanent members of the UN Security Council, should work together on global challenges and help maintain world peace and stability.

Putin also said the three countries shared interests in resolving regional conflicts, including the war in Ukraine, and in cooperating on economic ties, food and energy security, and counterterrorism.

100%US President Donald Trump, China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's President Vladimir Putin participate in a trilateral meeting during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, November 19, 2026Nov 19, 2026, 09:09 GMT+0Judge, wife and 3-year-old son killed in shooting in northwest IranA judge, his wife and their 3-year-old son were killed in a shooting in Tabriz, northwestern Iran, on Wednesday evening, state media reported Thursday.

Ebrahim Sadeghi, a judge from Piranshahr, was shot in Tabriz’s Heydarabad neighborhood. The assailant then shot himself and was taken to hospital with injuries, the report said.

The judge’s daughter, who was at the scene, survived after taking shelter in a nearby shop. The motive for the attack was under investigation, according to the report.

Iran’s budget for next year should prioritize strengthening the country’s military and economic capacity, a lawmaker said on Thursday.

“Military and economic strength must be a priority,” Ahmad Bigdeli told ILNA, adding that some development projects could be suspended temporarily.

He warned that otherwise Iran could face greater difficulties next year than during the war.

Belgium will seek to add the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen to the European Union’s terrorist list, following its efforts to have Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) listed, Defense Minister Theo Francken said on Thursday.

Francken said Belgium’s government had worked to secure the IRGC’s listing and would now pursue the same for Houthis. He praised Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot’s work on the effort.

“Our government has put a lot of effort in getting the IRGC on EU’s Terror List. Now we will do the same for Ansar Allah aka the Houthis. They are just another snake of the evil Medusaregime in Tehran,” Francken wrote on a post on X.

Trump also said the United States and China had divided tariffs fairly. He said a Board of Trade that the two leaders agreed to establish at their May summit in Beijing had brought balance to relations between the countries.

Before the meeting, Trump described it as likely to be productive.

Xi said he remained committed to working with Trump to keep China-US relations on the “correct course,” describing ties as stable and improving.
